name: Louis Wilkinson
bio: Louis Umfreville Wilkinson, a Radley schoolboy when he opened a correspondence with Wilde in the winter of 1898. To get into correspondence he invented an 'Ipswich Dramatic Society' and its wish to dramatise The Picture of Dorian Gray; the editors identify a second invention, his claim to have been at the first night of Lady Windermere's Fan, as made for the same purpose. A third claim was not invented but misattributed: it was his father, not he, who had known Edward FitzGerald, the two being neighbours in Suffolk. He and Wilde never met. Wilde, writing to Reggie Turner in January 1899, described him as 'a Radley schoolboy, aged seventeen'. He went up to Oxford, published many novels and other books under the name Louis Marlow, and in Seven Friends (1953) printed many of Wilde's letters to him, there confessing the Ipswich fabrication. His first letter to Wilde and some of the subsequent ones are in the Hyde Collection.
bio_note: All facts from Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000) with printed folios confirmed. Birth and death years, the Radley schooling, the Ipswich Dramatic Society fabrication, the pen-name Louis Marlow, Seven Friends (1953), the Hyde Collection provenance and the flat statement that the two never met are from the main-particulars footnote at p. 1109 n. 1 (the note begins on 1109 and concludes at the foot of 1110; PDF 1155-56, transcribed by the earlier record session). The Lady Windermere's Fan invention is p. 1127 n. 2 (PDF 1173). The FitzGerald correction is p. 1133 n. 1 (PDF 1179). The age is Wilde's own contemporaneous statement to Reginald Turner at p. 1118 (PDF 1164) and is consistent with the 1881 birth year. NOT read so far (pointers): the correspondence tail at printed 1136, 1159n, 1168, 1170-71 (Paris invitation) and 1171, and the funeral-wreath mention at approximately printed 1224.
